pk.context: 10 mg oral, single dose, healthy adults

pill.desc: white, round, bi-convex, film-coated extended-release tablet

tell: Its extended-release tablets give a 4.5-hour elimination half-life, against 3.2 hours for the immediate-release form.

clues.text: Oral bioavailability is 60% to 87%, and food has no significant effect on absorption. About 45% is bound to plasma protein, and it is cleared mainly by CYP3A metabolism and urinary excretion.
A hydrochloride salt, an odorless crystalline powder with a molecular weight of 315.4 for the active moiety.
Approved under an NDA in strengths from 10 mg to 80 mg, dosed every 12 hours.

Boxed warning on addiction, abuse and misuse, and on life-threatening respiratory depression. Contraindicated with known or suspected gastrointestinal obstruction; constipation, nausea and somnolence are common.
Severe, persistent pain that other treatment options cannot adequately manage, in adults and in selected pediatric patients 11 years of age and older.
It is a full agonist that is relatively selective for the mu receptor, though it can bind other opioid receptors at higher doses.
The generic name begins with O and has nine letters.
